title: Degree as a multiplicity-weighted sum over integral components
statement:
Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $X$ be proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism] with topological Krull dimension at most one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension], and let $\mathcal N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Let $C_1,\ldots,C_t$ be the irreducible components of dimension one [def-weil-irreducible-components], each equipped with its reduced induced closed subscheme structure (on an affine open this is the quotient by the prime ideal of the component) [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-closed-immersion]. This is a finite list; each $C_i$ is an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] proper over $k$ of dimension one. Let $\xi_i$ be its generic point, meaning $\overline{\{\xi_i\}}=C_i$, and put $m_i=\operatorname{length}_{\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i}}(\mathcal O_{X,\xi_i})$, using the stalk [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk] and module length [def-weil-pbc-module-length]. Each $m_i$ is a finite positive integer. Write $\mathcal N|_{C_i}=j_i^*\mathcal N$ for pullback along the closed immersion $j_i:C_i\to X$ [def-pc-module-pullback]. With $\deg_k(\mathcal P)=\chi(Y,\mathcal P)-\chi(Y,\mathcal O_Y)$ on any proper $Y/k$ [def-pc-degree-line-bundle, def-pc-euler-characteristic], one has
$$\deg_k(\mathcal N)=\sum_{i=1}^t m_i\deg_k(\mathcal N|_{C_i}).$$
The sum is zero when $t=0$, including when $X$ is empty or has dimension at most zero.

source.place: Tag 0AYW, lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components, rank-one specialization; multiplicity definition immediately before the lemma.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-curve-integral-filtration-multiplicity-profile] to $X$. It gives the finite list of reduced integral proper dimension-one components and their unique generic points, including the affine prime-ideal description. It also gives coherence of $\mathcal O_X$ and a coherent integral-ideal filtration $0=\mathcal F_0\subseteq\cdots\subseteq\mathcal F_s=\mathcal O_X$, with quotients $\mathcal Q_a\cong(h_a)_*\mathcal I_a$. Every support is either a one-point dimension-zero scheme or one of the $C_i$ as a reduced closed subscheme. In this filtration $m_i$ is a finite positive integer equal to $\#\{a:h_a(Z_a)=C_i\}$.

source.place: Tag 0AYW (lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components), coherent-filtration assembly of the original proof.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-trf-integral-filtration-euler-difference] to $\mathcal F=\mathcal O_X$ and the filtration just obtained. Its hypotheses on coherence, properness, integral supports and dimensions are supplied by Step 1. The unit isomorphism $\mathcal N\otimes\mathcal O_X\cong\mathcal N$, $n\otimes f\mapsto fn$, and [def-pc-degree-line-bundle] identify its Euler difference with degree. Thus
$$\deg_k(\mathcal N)=\sum_{a:\dim Z_a=1}\deg_k(h_a^*\mathcal N).$$
The cited lemma includes the tensor and cohomology identifications and the vanishing of each zero-dimensional factor.

source.place: Tag 0AYW (lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components), coherent-filtration assembly of the original proof.

proof.text:
For each dimension-one factor, the identification $Z_a=C_i$ over $X$ in Step 1 identifies $h_a^\ast\mathcal N$ with $j_i^\ast\mathcal N$. Regroup the finite sum of Step 2 by these supports and use the counts of Step 1:
$$\deg_k(\mathcal N)=\sum_{i=1}^t\#\{a:h_a(Z_a)=C_i\}\deg_k(j_i^*\mathcal N)=\sum_{i=1}^t m_i\deg_k(\mathcal N|_{C_i}).$$
If $t=0$, Step 1 leaves only zero-dimensional factors, so the sum of Step 2 is empty. When $X$ is empty its structure module is zero and Step 1 allows the length-zero filtration, covered by Step 2. This proves every stated empty-sum case.

source.place: Tag 0AYW (lemma-degree-in-terms-of-components), coherent-filtration assembly of the original proof.
